title: The ideal Otto cycle, compression ratio 10
caption: 1→2 adiabatic compression from V to V/10 (pressure × 25.1), 2→3 heat in at constant volume, 3→4 adiabatic expansion, 4→1 heat out at constant volume. With γ = 1.4, η = 1 − r^(1−γ) = 1 − 10^−0.4 = 60.2%, found here also from heat in ∝ p₃ − p₂ and heat out ∝ p₄ − p₁ (60.2%). Real engines reach about 35%.
alt: p–V diagram of the Otto cycle: two adiabats joined by two vertical constant-volume lines, volume ratio 10; efficiency 60 percent.
description: Axes: volume as a multiple of the clearance volume, pressure as a multiple of the intake pressure p₁.
1→2: adiabatic compression from V = 10 to 1: p rises from 1 to 25.1 (pV^1.4 constant).
2→3: combustion at constant volume, p to 75.4. 3→4: adiabatic expansion back to V = 10, p = 3.0. 4→1: exhaust heat at constant volume.
